title: Prove unchanged relationships at open, and stop rebuilding what the source already carries
code_state: crates/litchi-opc only: src/rel.rs, src/package.rs, src/pkgwriter.rs, src/atomic.rs
reason_codes: the publication plan reserialized and XML-audited the .rels of every part with relationships, and rebuilt and audited [Content_Types].xml, on every save regardless of whether anything had changed; try_write_preserved then byte-compared the result and raw-copied the source member, so the audited bytes never reached the output

the open already serializes every part's relationships into the preservation provenance, so the proof the save needs exists before the save begins; binding it to the live collection behind an Arc and clearing it on every mutation makes the unchanged case decidable in one pointer comparison
measured per publish on the 132-member workbook with every member unchanged: 42 verify_authored calls to 0, 78 try_to_xml_bytes calls to 0, 992,747 native cycles to 342,567 (-65.49%)

SAVE-2's write-syscall reduction is deterministic and large (531 to 14 write(2) calls for the same 654,681 bytes and the same output digest), but its modelled 0.8-1.6 ms latency gain is falsified on this host: save(path) is fsync-bound and the measured p50 effect is -2.33%, inside the host's stated 4% p50 floor

intentional_behaviour_change.what: the authored-XML audit of generated bytes that are then discarded no longer runs for an unchanged .rels collection or an unchanged content-types manifest
intentional_behaviour_change.reachability: a save would have to be refused today by verify_authored under Limits::default() on XML this code generates and never publishes; the only resource path is the auditor's 250,000 aggregate attribute ceiling against ReadLimits' 100,000 relationships per part, so roughly 62,500 relationships on one part
intentional_behaviour_change.why accepted: the published bytes are unchanged on every input; the refusal was already inconsistent, because the same package opened and saved without any mutation takes the exact-source path and audits nothing; the bytes copied in its place passed the reader's own relationship count, size, event, depth and attribute limits at open; audits of changed members are untouched (ADR 0006, record 0528)
intentional_behaviour_change.precedent: 0519 recorded an intentional refusal-behaviour change of the same shape inside an implemented record

api_change.what: litchi_opc::atomic::replace and replace_with hand their closure &mut AtomicSink<'_> instead of &mut File
api_change.why: the 64 KiB staging buffer has to live inside replace_with_impl so every format's save(path) benefits and so caller-supplied sinks are never wrapped
api_change.blast_radius: six in-tree call sites in litchi-opc, litchi-xlsx, litchi-docx and litchi-pptx; all use the argument as a Write sink and compile unchanged

accepted_evidence.corpus_oracle: 336 OOXML fixtures (180 xlsx, 78 pptx, 62 docx, 15 xlsb, 1 dotx) x 4 mutation scenarios = 1,344 rows of published length plus SHA-256, or the typed error; before and after outputs are byte-identical (corpus-diff.txt is empty), including 27 preserved save refusals and 8 preserved open refusals
accepted_evidence.editor_oracle: tabs and edit_cells over three fixtures x four operations on both legs; 12 of 12 rows identical, including the two pre-existing NotCompact refusals 0587 reported
accepted_evidence.counts: callgrind isolation pairs (M=10) for per-publish call counts and Ir on four fixtures x three scenarios; whole-process call counts for the two real editor saves; strace -s 0 write and fsync counts on the real save(path) route
accepted_evidence.cycles: native perf stat isolation pairs (M=200, -r 5) for cycles and instructions on four fixture/scenario pairs
accepted_evidence.timing: paired A1 B1 B2 A2, 2,000 samples per leg-run with 200 warmups for publish-only, 100 samples per leg-run for the atomic save(path) route, all pinned to CPU 13, with the A/A floor taken from the A1/A2 pair in the same window
accepted_evidence.tests: 9 new tests in litchi-opc, including a differential that publishes the same package through the pristine route and through the forced serialize-and-compare route and requires identical bytes
accepted_evidence.gates: cargo fmt --all --check; cargo clippy -p litchi-opc --all-targets; cargo test -p litchi-opc; cargo doc -p litchi-opc --no-deps; cargo clippy and cargo test for litchi-xlsx, litchi-docx and litchi-pptx; all exit 0 with no failures

accepted_costs.shared_host: seven other agents were building and measuring throughout; run-window load average 35-44 on 32 cores
accepted_costs.tails_unusable: the p99 A/A floor in the timing window was -38.54% to +99.40% because of ~3.1 ms scheduling stalls; only p50 is interpreted, against a measured p50 A/A floor of -0.57% to +0.66%
accepted_costs.instruction_accounting: callgrind counts rep movsb and memcmp per byte, so the unchanged bulk-copy share is inflated and the callgrind percentages (-27% to -61%) are the conservative view against the native cycle percentages (-62% to -71%)
accepted_costs.no_harness_selector: tools/perf-baseline has no ordinary-save selector and adding one would change its checked catalog SHA-256, selector registry and coverage-index minimum; a scratch probe with path dependencies was used and is retained with its manifest template
accepted_costs.scratch_probe_lockfile: the probe was built without --locked because it is a fresh crate; both legs resolve the same dependency versions through the same path dependencies

known_gaps.semantic_editors: no DOCX or PPTX semantic-editor save was measured through Path A, because no example opens a real .docx or .pptx, edits through the model and saves (0587 section 4); those 140 fixtures are covered at the OpcPackage level by the corpus oracle only
known_gaps.unreachable_path: PublicationPlan::materialize_pristine cannot be reached today, because a package with pristine members is refused with PreservationUnavailable before the full writer runs; it is guarded by a typed error rather than by a test
known_gaps.unmeasured: cold-cache behaviour, peak RSS, real-device fsync distributions, packages larger than 132 members, and the 62,500-relationship refusal boundary, which is arithmetic and was not constructed

withheld: any registered claim, cold-cache, physical-device, peak-RSS, allocation-profile, concurrency-scaling, cross-platform or tail-latency result

provenance.host: AMD EPYC 9R45, 32 cores, 123 GiB, Linux 7.0.0-1012-aws, rustc 1.95.0, cargo 1.95.0, valgrind 3.26.0
provenance.build: cargo build --release --locked, workspace profile lto = true and panic = abort, separate CARGO_TARGET_DIR per leg
